Launch WAC was $1,850 a month, which BMS put at $22,500 a year (CNBC 2024-09-26; BioPharma Dive; BMS UK pricing statement, bms.com/news-and-media/statements/cobenfy-uk-pricing.html)
column12: Judgement: a published list price for the comparator, not for direclidine. The brief ranks a named list price above the CMS convention. Cobenfy is the closest marketed comparator: it is the only muscarinic agonist on the market, it treats the same disease, and its label (schizophrenia in adults, BMY FY2025 10-K 0000014272-26-000004) is the one direclidine's acute inpatient programme would produce. The CMS convention cannot be read for Cobenfy: lookup.py demand Cobenfy shows Part D 2024 at $2,359,550 over 961 beneficiaries, $2,455 each, and that is its launch quarter only (US launch October 2024). Case for lower: BMS said Cobenfy is priced 'in line with existing branded oral schizophrenia treatments' (BioPharma Dive, via search), but Vraylar's 2024 list was $1,376 per 30 days (CMS IPAY 2027 fact sheet), 27% below Cobenfy's current WAC. Its CMS Part D figure is $9,662 per beneficiary in 2024 (lookup.py demand Vraylar), and Caplyta's is $9,940. A second entrant to the class may also price at or below the first. Case for higher: a once-daily pill with no trospium may be positioned at parity or at a premium to a twice-daily one

column11: CMS, Medicare Drug Price Negotiation Program, negotiated prices for initial price applicability year 2027 (cms.gov/files/document/fact-sheet-negotiated-prices-ipay-2027.pdf): Vraylar list price $1,376 per 30-day supply (2024), negotiated price $770, a 44% discount. The $770 is in the book (negotiated_prices, VRAYLAR, mfp_30des 770, effective 2027-01-01, source cms_mfp). 1 - 770/1,376 = 0.4404
column12: Judgement. A WAC anchor takes neither house convention, so the discount must be sourced, and this is the only published list-to-net discount found for a branded oral antipsychotic in schizophrenia. Direction checked: 44.04% comes off list, so net is $12,848 per patient-year. Case for a smaller discount: CMS negotiated the price for a drug a decade past launch, and gross_to_net.py calls such a price conservative for a fresh launch. Antipsychotics are also a protected Part D class with thin rebates. Case for a larger discount: BMS puts more than 80% of schizophrenia patients on Medicare or Medicaid (BioPharma Dive, via search). Medicaid takes a statutory 23.1% basic rebate plus supplemental and inflation rebates, and from 2025 Part D adds a 10% to 20% manufacturer discount. The book's other WAC discount, 0.2777 from Kalydeco, is not used: its own row calls it a floor that mostly measures fill coverage, and it comes from cystic fibrosis

column12: Constant hazard: 1 - (1 - 1061/1432)^(12/18) = 0.5936 a year. This is the class's reference measure of all-cause discontinuation, in the label's population, on oral daily antipsychotics. Case for higher: the muscarinic class so far keeps fewer patients. In EMERGENT-4, 34 of the 156 who enrolled in the 52-week xanomeline-trospium extension completed it, 21.8%, so 78.2% stopped (Kaul I et al., Am J Psychiatry 2026;183(3):183-192, doi:10.1176/appi.ajp.20241186, PMID 41634905). Case for lower: EMERGENT-5 reported 51% withdrawal over 52 weeks (a secondary figure, from the review by Ji F et al., Ther Adv Psychopharmacol 2026, doi:10.1177/20451253261478086, PMID 42621264). Direclidine avoids trospium and the twice-daily schedule, which may improve persistence. The same rate is used to back out Cobenfy's new starts in penetration_peak_pct, so the two stay consistent

column11: Primary completion NCT06963034 2027-10 and NCT07105098 2027-11, both estimated (book trials table). Precedent: Karuna submitted the KarXT NDA in September 2023 and the FDA approved Cobenfy on 26 September 2024, a standard 12-month review (Karuna NDA acceptance release, 2023-11-29, via search; BMY FY2024 10-K 0000014272-25-000039). That approval rested on acute placebo-controlled trials plus open-label safety data of up to one year (BMY FY2024 10-K)
column12: Judgement on the timeline. Topline around the turn of 2028, an NDA about six months later, and a standard review put approval around mid-2029, so 2030 is the first full year. Neither the relapse-prevention study (2029-07) nor the long-term study (2031-12) should gate the filing, since Cobenfy was approved without a relapse-prevention study. The long-term study began in July 2025, so one-year exposures exist by 2028. Case for 2029: the book's usual rule, the second calendar year after primary completion, gives 2029, and a filing early in 2028 would leave most of 2029 on market. Case for 2031: a failure in one acute study would mean running another.

column11: Finnerty et al., 'Prevalence and incidence measures for schizophrenia among commercial health insurance and medicaid enrollees', npj Schizophrenia 2024;10:68, doi:10.1038/s41537-024-00490-0, PMID 39174558, PMC11341906 (read in full). In IBM MarketScan, 712 of 951,173 people continuously insured from 2009 to 2019 had a new diagnosis of schizophrenia in 2019, 0.07% (95% CI 0.07-0.08): two or more claims for schizophrenia or schizoaffective disorder (ICD-10 F20, F25; schizophreniform excluded) in 2019 and no schizophrenia diagnosis in the prior ten years, a look-back the paper validates as its reference standard. Applied to the adult base the book's prevalence row implies (1,200,448 / 0.445% = 269,763,596): 269,763,596 x 712/951,173 = 201,931
column12: Judgement: a commercially insured rate applied to all US adults. POPULATION IT COUNTS: new claims diagnoses of schizophrenia or schizoaffective disorder among employer-insured people of every age with ten years of unbroken coverage and at least one service a year. It is diagnosed incidence, not onset, and narrower in diagnosis than the book's prevalence, which includes related psychotic disorders. Case for higher: in the same study NYS Medicaid ran 1,489 of 785,088 (0.19%), 511,634 a year on this base, and people with schizophrenia are concentrated in Medicaid. Case for lower: 201,931 is 16.8% of the carried prevalence, about six years of diagnosed illness for a lifelong disease, so some 'new' F20/F25 diagnoses are people the NIMH figure already counts under related psychotic disorders; the paper's schizophrenia-only rate (75 per 100,000) is above the chart-confirmed first-episode psychosis rate for ages 30-59 in five US health systems (46 per 100,000, Simon et al., Psychiatr Serv 2017, PMID 28045349, PMC5811263), which counts every psychosis. Cross-check: Teixeira et al. (PLoS One 2022, PMID 36137136) found 1.04 per 1,000 Optum adults newly diagnosed with schizophrenia disorders in 2020; Finnerty's MarketScan PPV of 81% at a one-year look-back takes that to about 0.84 per 1,000, near this 0.75. ENGINE WARNING: forecast.derive_new_patients adds incidence x eligible_pct to the untreated pool every year with no deaths. At this inflow and the re-solved peak the untreated pool passes the NIMH high end (1,726,486) in 2032 and reaches 3.88mm by 2044, and revenue climbs without a plateau to about $801mm in 2044. An untreated_carryover_pct of prevalence / (prevalence + incidence) = 0.8560 holds the pool at the carried prevalence (stock tops out near 22,100, about $284mm); it is not set here because no source states it. Carry this figure in epidemiology.csv rather than on this asset alone, so no second schizophrenia asset carries a different one

column11: Label basis: Cobenfy is 'indicated for the treatment of schizophrenia in adults' (BMY FY2025 10-K 0000014272-26-000004), approved on EMERGENT-2/-3. Those trials enrolled adults aged 18-65 recently hospitalised for worsening psychosis, with PANSS of 80 or more and CGI-S of 4 or more (EMERGENT-2, Kaul I et al., Lancet 2024;403:160-170, doi:10.1016/S0140-6736(23)02190-6, PMID 38104575). Direclidine's Phase 3 acute studies use the same acute inpatient design (NCT06963034, NCT07105098: 'Inpatient Adults With Schizophrenia', PANSS at week 5)
column12: Judgement. In schizophrenia the Phase 3 entry criteria (acute exacerbation, inpatient, PANSS 80 or more) do not carry into the label: the same design gave Cobenfy an all-adults label. The drug has no biomarker, and no line of therapy is stated. The book's pool is already adults. No filter is applied, for two reasons. The pool's excess over the label (related psychotic disorders, and the untreated) has no sourced share. And penetration_peak_pct is solved from Cobenfy on this same 1.0 basis, so any filter here would scale the solved peak up by the same factor and leave patients almost unchanged. Case for a filter: the label reaches schizophrenia only, and a patient outside care cannot be started

column11: Cobenfy, measured from BMS's filed US net sales: $10mm in FY2024 (launch October 2024), $155mm in FY2025 (10-K 0000014272-26-000004, all US) and $119mm in H1 2026 ($56mm in Q1, $63mm in Q2; 8-Ks 0000014272-26-000008 and -000018; book asset_revenue). Each is divided by the net price on the same basis as this seed: WAC ($1,850 per 30 days in 2024-2025, $1,887 in 2026) x 365/30 x (1 - 0.4404). That gives patient-years on therapy of 794 (2024), 12,306 (2025) and 18,525 (2026, H1 annualised). The engine's stock recursion at the 0.5936 stop rate backs out new starts of 11,983 in 2025 and 13,524 in 2026. The engine's eligible pool in a year is the untreated pool plus that year's incidence, so the 2026 capture is 13,524 over the book's pool less the patients already started (1,200,448 - 794 - 11,983 = 1,187,671) plus one year of the incidence set above (201,931): 13,524 / 1,389,603 = 0.9732%
column12: Judgement: 1.0x Cobenfy's second-full-year capture, used as the peak, re-solved at second read for the incidence added above (1.1387% on the same data with no inflow; use that figure if the incidence is not adopted). Cobenfy's new starts rose only 13% from 2025 to 2026 (11,983 to 13,524) while its revenue grew on the carried stock, so its capture looks near a plateau rather than early on a ramp. Case for higher: Cobenfy is still growing (Q2 2026 annualised gives 1.05% with the incidence); a 0.78 stop rate (EMERGENT-4) gives 1.14%, and a 0.5 discount 1.09%. The consensus peak the book carries for Cobenfy, $3.9bn (revenue_ceiling_musd), would need about 303,600 patient-years, new starts of some 15% of the prevalence a year. Neurocrine sells Ingrezza to the same psychiatrists, and a once-daily M4 agonist without trospium may tolerate better. Case for lower: direclidine is second into a class that BMS is still struggling to move past 'deeply ingrained D2 prescribing habits' (BMS Q3 2025 results, 8-K 0000014272-25-000147). Cobenfy's adjunctive ARISE study missed (BMY FY2025 10-K). Cobenfy's 2025 starts include a launch bolus of waiting switchers. The Kalydeco 0.2777 discount would give 0.75%. With the incidence and no exit from the pool the engine's stock does not settle: see the incidence note

column11: derived to hold the schizophrenia pool at its measured size, the method the remternetug seed uses: the book's prevalence (epidemiology.csv, NIMH, 1,200,448 x eligible_pct 1.0) and its inflow (201,931 a year, Finnerty 2024) are stationary only if exits equal entries, which sets retention at 1,200,448 / (1,200,448 + 201,931) = 0.8560
column12: JUDGEMENT. The engine models no exit from the untreated pool (deaths, remission, loss to care), so at full carryover the second reader measured it passing NIMH's high-end prevalence by 2032 and revenue still rising in 2044. Holding it stationary is the book's answer to the same problem on remternetug. The case against: diagnosed schizophrenia is lifelong for most, so the true exit rate is mortality (standardised mortality about 2.5 times the population's), lower than 14% a year, and the stationary pool understates a growing diagnosed population
